newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian police prepare to arrest "Bandit Queen".
newsitem.headline: Indian police prepare to arrest "Bandit Queen".

text.p: Indian police prepared on Sunday to arrest member of parliament and former "Bandit Queen" Phoolan Devi, who has ignored a summons to appear in court and is wanted in dozens of cases, including murder.
Uttar Pradesh state police chief Hari Das Rao said police were being deployed in the capital, New Delhi, to arrest Devi on Monday, when she must again appear in court.
"A large police contingent is being rushed to New Delhi for the purpose," Rao told Reuters. He said police expected Devi to go to New Delhi ahead of Thursdays opening session of parliament.
On February 4 Devi ignored a summons to appear in court, where she faced arrest warrants in 57 pending cases.
Indian police have issued a nationwide alert for her arrest and have been unable to track her down despite raids on two of her homes.

The government of the northern state of Uttar Pradesh, of which Lucknow is the capital, appealed 10 days ago to Indias Supreme Court to overturn the lower courts verdict. A hearing on the appeal is also scheduled for Monday.
Devis lawyer Nand Lal Jaiswal said Devi was not planning to surrender to the police.

"Why should I advise her to surrender when the state government has already moved the countrys apex court...to quash the governments earlier decision to withdraw each of the criminal cases registered against her?" Jaiswal told Reuters.

Movie maker Sekhar Kapoor portrayed Devi, who belongs to the low-caste Mallah community of boatmen, as a heroine in the biographical film "Bandit Queen" which won acclaim at several international film festivals.
Devi shot to notoriety after 22 upper-caste men were killed in a massacre at the northern Indian village of Behmai in 1981.
She was accused of leading a gang in the massacre but denied the charges.
Devi surrendered to the police in 1983 under an amnesty offered by the central state of Madhya Pradesh. She spent more than 10 years in prison before being released on parole in 1994.

The chief minister of Uttar Pradesh then withdrew all cases against her and inducted her into his Samajwadi Party, a regional socialist party which represents low castes. She easily won a constituency in elections last May.
The states high court revived the cases after a man who claimed to be one of her intended victims asked that they be reinstated.
On February 4, the court rejected a demand by Devis lawyer to withdraw the arrest warrants, and ordered police to produce her in court on February 17.
